title: COG (Cloud Optimized GeoTIFF) Provider
description: Raster tiles served via TiTiler from S3-hosted COG files. Best for continuous raster data (elevation, NDVI, climate indices).

body.source: Canonical single-COG source. Use an s3:// URI, e.g. s3://bucket/path/file.tif.
body.sources: Optional array of s3:// URIs for multi-source COG layers. When present, the frontend builds one TiTiler-backed tile layer per source and groups them.
body.url: Optional pre-built TiTiler tile URL template including {z}/{x}/{y}. Prefer source/sources for managed layers; use url only when the full TiTiler URL is already known.
body.colormap_name: Named colormap string, e.g. 'viridis', 'plasma', 'rdylgn'. Mutually exclusive with colormap.
body.colormap: Custom colormap. Two formats are supported: (1) gradient object {'0':[r,g,b,a],...} used with rescale, or (2) interval array [[[lo,hi],[r,g,b,a]], ...]. For interval arrays, do NOT also set rescale because TiTiler would normalize away the raw class values.
body.rescale: Array [min,max] for value-to-color mapping. Use with gradient colormaps and named colormaps. Omit for interval-array colormaps.
body.bidx: Band index (1-based integer). E.g. 1 for first band.
body.nodata: Value to treat as transparent, e.g. -9999 or 0.
body.clip_geometry: Optional GeoJSON geometry to clip the tile output before rendering.

options.tileSize: Optional tile size. Defaults to 256 in the frontend.

notes: COG files must be accessible from TiTiler — use public S3 objects or pre-signed URLs.
The S3 data bucket is public-read; use s3://bucket/path format for source.
TiTiler automatically handles reprojection and tiling.
For new raster layers, always upload to S3 first and get the s3:// URI.
interaction_config is required on Layer records. For COG layers, the canonical managed config uses the TiTiler point-query template with {{titilerUrl}} and {{cogUrl}} placeholders.
For analysis-capable COG layers, current validation allows analysis_type 'histogram' or 'categorical'.
